verdict.headline: Strait of Hormuz deal fractures as Iran moves to bar US ships, sending oil sharply higher
verdict.rationale_short: The Bessent Hormuz framework is fracturing: Iranian officials circulated a draft plan banning U.S. and Israeli commercial vessels from the Strait, reversing three days of oil deflation that had kept September hike odds contained. Brent at $83.46 is $1.54 from the $85 regime trigger; WTI at $78.05 puts the $79 oil-side gate in play before tomorrow's NFP. The constructive counter-signal is SPCX: Day-2 at ~$115 (+3%) after a Day-1 that held within a 3% band means the feared panic liquidation did not materialize — supply is being absorbed more cleanly than the staggered-lockup template implied. The 30Y at 5.20% remains the sole formal regime breach (1-of-6). Hold: the tape cannot price oil escalation and NFP simultaneously. Tomorrow's 8:30 AM ET print is the resolving event — below 70K collapses September hike odds and allows the 30Y to compress toward 5.00%; above 130K with oil still elevated risks 3-of-6 regime in 24 hours.

watchlist_mentions.note: Day-2 after lockup: ~$115, +3%. The feared mass liquidation on Day-1 did not materialize — Bloomberg confirms shares traded within a 3% band as the first 20% tranche (911.5M shares, ~$116B eligible) became available. Day-2 stabilization at $115 is constructively above the $93 distressed scenario modeled in earlier briefs and represents genuine absorption rather than a delayed selloff. The next structural supply event is the 7% staggered tranche in 2-4 weeks; the December 180-day release remains the terminal floor. Q3 Starlink earnings (~October 2026) is the only fundamental catalyst that can revalue the lockup supply overhang before December. Above $120 on volume would confirm the first 20% tranche was absorbed; below $105 on volume would signal the next wave of sellers is front-running the next tranche.

~$64,934, +0.57% (Crypto.com live as of 11:03 UTC). Session range $64,157–$64,989 — tight consolidation rather than directional positioning ahead of NFP. Gate 2 ($62,000) buffer intact at $2,934. Constructive signal: oil rising on Hormuz escalation has not triggered a crypto risk-off correlation — BTC is not tracking the geopolitical bid in crude. A cross-asset risk-off would require simultaneous equity deterioration beyond 7,380 SPX, not currently in view.

~$220, holding through the Hormuz oil move and unchanged from the prior session's level. The August 26 Q2 FY27 print (gross margin target 76%+, datacenter revenue above consensus) is the defining event for the $216 structural support level. Polysilicon Section 232 tariffs (15%) affect NVDA indirectly via downstream supply chain cost pressure on solar/data-center build partners — a second-order watch item rather than a direct catalyst. Divergence from MU/SKHY (still in bear-market territory from July highs) holds: if this is supply-layer noise in HBM, NVDA holds $216; if AI capex peaking is the driver, the divergence closes before August 26.

trade_setups.asset: NFP binary — July payrolls Friday 8:30 AM ET
trade_setups.thesis: The July NFP print (consensus 83K, prior 57K) is the session's dominant variable and will reprice the Hormuz+rate-hike stack simultaneously. With September hike probability at 54% and the 30Y at 5.20% (sole regime breach), the print has a non-linear policy impact: below 70K confirms ADP's 44K signal (softest of 2026, well below the 75K consensus) and should compress September odds toward 35–40%, allowing the 30Y to retrace toward 5.00% and resolve the regime's only breach. Above 130K alongside sticky Brent above $83 re-prices September toward 65–70% and risks pushing the regime from 1-of-6 to 3-of-6 in a single 24-hour window.
trade_setups.entry: September hike probability on Kalshi within 10 minutes of the 8:30 AM ET release is the lead indicator. Below 40%: compression thesis active, constructive posture on rate-sensitives. Above 65%: regime expansion risk, posture shifts toward step_aside. The 7,380 SPX floor remains the structural backstop regardless of print direction.
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP at 83–100K (in-line) is the ambiguous scenario: hike odds remain 50–58%, oil continues as the dominant driver, and the regime stays in current 1-of-6 configuration with no catalyst for directional resolution. Hold posture extends through the following week.
trade_setups.horizon: Binary event: Friday 8:30 AM ET. Posture resolution: 1-2 sessions post-print.

trade_setups.asset: Brent Crude — Hormuz $85 regime trigger watch
trade_setups.thesis: The Iranian draft plan banning US and Israeli vessels from the Strait is a break from the Bessent-mediated framework that had kept Brent below $80 for three sessions. At $83.46, Brent is $1.54 from the $85 regime trigger that would add a second formal breach alongside the 30Y. A breach of $85 before the NFP print would move the regime to 2-of-6 regardless of what payrolls shows, warranting a posture shift toward step_aside in energy-cost-sensitive names (consumer discretionary, airlines, industrials).
trade_setups.entry: Brent $85 is the formal trigger; WTI $79 is the companion gate. A Hormuz agreement signed in the next 12–24 hours that restores the Bessent framework collapses Brent back toward $78–79 and removes this setup entirely. Absent that, the risk-reward favors being underweight energy-cost-exposed sectors into the NFP print rather than waiting for the double-trigger.
trade_setups.invalidation: Hormuz deal signed or Iranian government retracts the draft plan: Brent compresses below $80, oil gates clear, and the sole remaining breach is 30Y at 5.20%. Any Bessent statement before Friday open is the event to watch.
trade_setups.horizon: Oil-side resolution: 24–48 hours pending diplomatic clarity. NFP overlay: Friday 8:30 AM ET.

bear_case: NFP prints above 130K Friday while Hormuz remains unresolved: September hike probability breaks 70% (second breach), Brent holds above $85 (third breach), and the 30Y extends above 5.20% — a 3-of-6 regime configuration in a single 24-hour window that the current hold posture cannot survive. SPCX Day-2 stability is the bull case's only clean read; if Day-3 (Monday) deteriorates back below $105 on volume, the staggered lockup is front-running rather than absorbing, and the AI-infrastructure equity complex loses its anchoring signal heading into NVDA's August 26 earnings. The polysilicon Section 232 tariff is a slow-burn risk that has not yet been priced into semiconductor supply chains — it is not a trigger today but may compound the Hormuz/NFP stack if tech guidance in August earnings references it.
